ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set lambda=0 while retaining 32 Poincare anchors and identical optimizer/data/training schedule.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use train-only q-weighted Poincare assignment with fixed c=1 and 32 anchors; compare all three arms under identical 3000-epoch Stage2 and frozen Stage3 protocol.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Replace every first-level d_c squared distance with squared Euclidean distance, retain q, lambda, 32 anchors and matched parameter count.
ideas.behavior_computation: From train.parquet only, count consecutive (previous item,target item) pairs within each user's training sequence; map previous items to fixed embedding clusters and form q_i,g=(count(i,g)+alpha)/(sum_g count(i,g)+alpha G). Never read validation or test rows.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed immediate item transitions, summarized as predecessor-cluster distributions for each target item.
ideas.cost_estimate: Precompute the transition/cohort table once; per epoch cached behavior cost is O(N*32*8) (~6.3M scalar distance contributions), plus baseline training. The uncached upper bound is ~151M contributions/epoch; at 24 steps, compute b only on the item minibatch and cache detached costs for the epoch. Expected modest memory for N*32 float costs (~3.1M values, 12 MB); no extra Stage3 cost.
ideas.coupling_equation: z_i=argmin_{k in [32]} {d_c(x_i,a_k)^2 + lambda sum_g q_i,g d_c(a_k,p_g)^2}; q_i,g is the behavior term and d_c is the curved term.
ideas.coupling_path: Each target's train-derived cohort distribution weights geodesic distance to cohort prototypes, changing the argmin over trainable curved first-level anchors; removing q or replacing d_c changes the same assignment.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Similar predecessor cohorts have compact neighborhoods in negative curvature, and 32 curved anchors can improve first-prefix predictability without erasing useful distinctions. Keep only if canonical 52,855-pair/10-fixed-negative L1 Hard ER remains informative, gold-prefix survival through depths 1–3 rises, T4 NLL remains near constant, and frozen-protocol Stage3 test_R@10 exceeds 0.065.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: First-level anchor learning and assignment during Stage2 quantization; residual levels remain baseline Euclidean and T4 remains deterministic collision extension.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Squared Poincare distance d_c^2 at fixed negative curvature -c (c=1), with expmap0 for anchor/prototype parameterization and projection to radius (1-eps)/sqrt(c).
ideas.key_change: Build each item's smoothed distribution over its training-only predecessor cohorts, map cohort prototypes into the Poincare ball, and optimize 32 first-level anchors against both item embeddings and those prototypes using one geodesic assignment cost. Residual Euclidean RQ-VAE stages encode remaining item detail.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Construct transitions and q only from train interactions; item embeddings/clusters are frozen Stage1 content artifacts, not derived from validation/test interactions. Validation/test are used only after SID freezing for evaluation.
ideas.motivation: The beam loses targets when early prefixes branch too widely, yet a useful first token must group items likely to follow similar training histories.
ideas.novelty: Learn first-level anchors from behavior-conditioned cohort prototypes, rather than applying a behavior penalty to a fixed Euclidean quantizer. Cohort evidence moves the curved anchors themselves; the first-level budget is explicitly 32 groups.
ideas.observables: Report L1 Hard ER on the canonical 52,855 pairs with ten fixed negatives; gold-prefix survival at depths 1,2,3,4; T4 NLL; Stage3 test_R@10. Capacity target: T1 ≤5 bits, T2/T3 carry item discrimination, T4 <0.1 nats. Predict L1 ER lower than 256-way baseline but nonzero, depth-1 survival higher, depth-2/3 survival higher, T4 NLL approximately unchanged, and Recall@10 >0.065.

ideas.safeguards: Use alpha smoothing, q top-8 renormalization, epsilon denominators, Poincare projection, float32 distance accumulation, clamp sinh/arcosh arguments, gradient clipping, and a fixed no-history prior. ideas.spec_equations: q_i,g as above; map Euclidean item vector u_i to x_i=exp_0^c(u_i); parameterize anchor raw vectors v_k and prototypes r_g, map with exp_0^c; compute C_ik=d_c(x_i,a_k)^2+lambda sum_g q_i,g d_c(a_k,p_g)^2; hard SID token argmin_k C_ik, with soft assignment during training. Use standard residual quantization on x_i after subtracting the selected first-level reconstruction in the existing baseline space.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are frozen item embeddings, train-only sequences, cluster map, and Stage2 minibatch. Output is one of 32 T1 tokens per item, updated encoder/anchors, and unchanged baseline T2/T3 plus deterministic T4.

specification.text: For each training item i, let q_i be its normalized smoothed distribution over predecessor-item clusters (clusters obtained by spherical k-means on frozen training item embeddings; include only directed transitions in train). Let a_k be trainable Poincare anchors, and p_g fixed Poincare embeddings of predecessor clusters. Define b_ik = sum_g q_ig d_c(a_k,p_g)^2 / (sum_g q_ig + eps). Assign z_i=argmin_k [d_c(x_i,a_k)^2 + lambda b_ik], with 32 anchors; train the encoder and anchors by the same softmin expected cost plus standard VQ commitment/reconstruction losses. Quantize residuals at L2/L3 with the baseline Euclidean residual quantizer; T4 remains collision extension only. Budget: T1 at most log2(32)=5 bits, T2/T3 share the remaining discriminative budget (target combined 8–10 nats), T4 target <0.1 nats. At the frozen scale, precompute q and prototypes once; assignment work is O(24*24556*32*G) only if dense, so store q sparse top-8 and calculate O(24*24556*32*8) scalar distances; roughly 151M distance terms/epoch and 453B over 3000 epochs, but only the first-layer warmup/assignment pass (e.g. evaluate b once per epoch and cache) reduces this to 151M terms total per epoch plus negligible anchor updates. This should be benchmarked; cache b_ik per epoch and refresh once per epoch.

objective:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.

## What Issue #125 measured, and what the next mechanism must change

#125 ran a read-only forensics pass over the four existing arms and the resample
reference, on all 57,439 test rows at the production width-20 beam:

* Recall@10 tracks **whether the target SID survives the beam at all**: for 91–93% of rows
  the target's complete SID is absent from all twenty beams in every arm, and
  duplicate/seen filtering plus the fallback fill contribute zero hits.
* The three single-first-code arms have `L1 Hard ER = 1.000` by construction while their
  Recall@10 spans 0.0467–0.0623, and their gold first token survives 100% of the time.
* Where the information sits decides everything: `l1_br` (0.0467) pushes it into T4
  (16,462 distinct values, 9.03 nats, depth-4 survival 0.068); `l1_br_euclid` (0.0621)
